page.layout: One page of text: woodcut ornament band at top, then a centred title and year, then a verse poem in one column of italic lines with a large decorated initial; a word "Autum" at the lower right margin continues the text. No running head, no page number.

main_text.head: Rogat BEZAM vt hortum suum inuisere velit. anno 1597.
main_text.p: E, Beza, nostri Visere blandulas Iucunditates nunc iuuet hortuli, Dum lenis auras Vere Fauonius Tepente mulcet, pulchrior Chloris Ornat venustis rura coloribus, Pictisque opacas floribus arbores.
Dum Vite colles Pampinea virent, Nouisque sylua luxuriant comis, Et molle abactis frigoribus pecus, Tenella gestit gramina carpere Apesque certant prouida Hymettio Replere caras nectare cellulas.
Dum saua Progne deflet Itym suum, Et torua paruo gutture Daulias Carmen recludens dulcius, amulos Vincit Volucrum nobilior choros.
Nunc cuncta ridsimilar nunc per agros triplex Ludit renidens Gratia. Mox Leo Mox Virgo, feruensque Andromedae pater Aestum reducent flammiferum: simul Autum

page.notes: The initial letter is a large woodcut "I" (decorated); read as "E" in the first line is the printed initial word start. Line "Nunc cuncta ridiculed" and "Ludit" line are partly uncertain; "ridant" likely intended. The final word "Autum" is cut off at the page edge and may be "Autumnum". Long s rendered as plain s; italic verse lines marked in the original as italic throughout.
